claims.statement: jev-grep is a local streaming CLI with remote inference; ast-grep and agrind run in explicit external pipelines rather than being spawned internally.
The runtime has no repository index, persistence, or response cache; its source-name HashMap only locates in-memory accounting slots and repeated uncapped input is evaluated again.
run owns invocation orchestration, one Api, stdout lock, aggregate found state and shared code-source accounting, while search and Reader own fresh physical-input state.
Inputs and model evaluations are processed sequentially using a nonparallel ignore walker and blocking HTTP client, with no concurrent inference or explicitly sorted directory order.
Clap parsing precedes run and owns required/typed arguments, accepted format values, help/version and declared conflicts; run performs additional semantic validation.

Runtime validation rejects blank query/model, nonfinite or out-of-range thresholds, invalid byte limits, zero timeout or max-count, duplicate stdin paths, --no-filename, and simultaneous --json and --format.
API URL, model and optional key resolve from explicit flags before JEV_GREP environment values before defaults; LG variables are ignored and no configuration-file loader exists in the runtime.
Defaults are the Zen systemone endpoint, jev-1.13 model, text input, human output, 0.5 thresholds, 16384-byte line and fragment limits, and a 30-second per-evaluation timeout.
Absent explicit paths, terminal stdin defaults to '.' and nonterminal stdin to '-'; explicit paths replace this default and can contain at most one stdin marker.

Api is constructed before input processing, validates HTTP/HTTPS without URL credentials, disables redirects and automatic reqwest retries, and sends input text to the configured endpoint only when evaluated.
Non-stdin discovery skips nonregular files, does not follow symlinks, excludes hidden entries by default, and --no-ignore disables ordinary/Git/global/exclude/parent ignore processing.

Glob overrides are rooted in the current working directory and checked on files after traversal rather than installed on WalkBuilder, so they do not restore entries excluded by hidden or ignore traversal.
Invalid globs, traversal errors and file-open errors abort processing; stdin is locked and files are read through BufReader.

Every physical input gets a fresh Reader with reset coordinates and the invocation-wide format, with no content sniffing; physical reads are bounded to max-line-bytes plus one overflow-detection byte and limits include line endings.
Text preserves original endings and requires NUL-free UTF-8; log-jsonl decodes an object string text field while retaining physical coordinates and rejecting physical or decoded NUL.
Native ast-grep candidates are schema/range validated and fragment-size checked before inference; they are evaluated independently without joining or splitting.
Text/log search retains one pending fragment, saved probability and split flag per physical input, so fragments do not join across input boundaries.

Text/log search evaluates the first record singly, then groups a fitting next record; either relation score at the join threshold extends the fragment with match_extended, otherwise it finalizes the old saved score and uses match_next for the new pending fragment.

Text/log extension exceeding the byte budget finalizes the old fragment with split metadata and evaluates the next record singly; oversized individual records error, EOF finalizes pending state, and idle input does not flush it.
Grouped API evaluations validate all four answers before returning scores, preventing partial responses from mutating pending fragment state.

Code-source accounting is shared across physical inputs by candidate file, tracks count and listing flags in first-seen order, and grows with upstream source cardinality rather than retaining a corpus.
For ast-grep, max-count caps selected candidates per upstream source and skips inference after the cap while still validating and size-checking every later candidate.
Ast-grep files-with-matches lists each upstream source once while continuing scanning, and count output includes zero-count sources in first-seen order only after successful completion of all inputs.

For text/log, counts and max-count are per physical input and files-with-matches stops that input at its first selection; quiet suppresses output and stops the entire invocation after the first completed selection.
Selection uses inclusive probability >= threshold, inverted by -v, and human and JSONL outputs share the same selection decision.

Search emitters own publication through run's shared stdout lock and explicitly flush selected results/listings; text/log counts flush per input or early limit and code counts defer to invocation completion.
The filename-prefix hint is ignored by search, so located human output includes source and ranges regardless of -H or -n; JSON output is located-fragment JSONL rather than ripgrep events.

Each API evaluation shares one timeout across at most four attempts, retry sleeps and response reading; only selected transient failures retry, while oversized responses, malformed JSON, missing answers and invalid probabilities fail without fallback decisions.
Errors stop subsequent processing without retracting prior flushed output, do not finalize pending fragments, and prevent deferred code-count publication.
Runtime success with selections exits 0 and no selections exits 1; errors print the contextual jev-grep diagnostic and exit 2 except any error chain containing an io BrokenPipe exits 0 silently.

Offline CLI tests protect precedence, traversal filters, selection modes, pending streaming/retry behavior, shared source accounting and BrokenPipe; reader and API unit tests protect coordinates, malformed records, group validation and evaluation deadlines.
